title: Treat the browser as another process
why: The screen runs far from the server. It renders elements, styles them, and listens for events.
outcome: Build one labeled input, button, and output with keyboard operation.

steps.title: Elements, rules, listeners
steps.question: What are the browser's three pieces?
explanation: HTML elements for structure, CSS rules for presentation, and event listeners for interaction. A wrong selector is found by inspecting the DOM, not by reinstalling packages.
Reference preview: frontend/index.html mounts the application root (lines 1-12); frontend/src/main.tsx renders into it (lines 6-10). Your practice page starts as plain HTML and gains structure later.

steps.title: See input, button, output
steps.question: How does the output know what to show?
explanation: The listener reads the input, computes, and writes the output region. Labels connect each control to its purpose for sighted, keyboard, and screen-reader users alike.
hints: Point at the label.
Point at the listener.
Compare with a form.
Read the expected result before you change code.

steps.title: Native first
steps.question: Why native controls before libraries?
explanation: Native input, button, and output bring keyboard support, focus outlines, and semantics free. Libraries add styling and behavior later without re-teaching interaction.

steps.title: Install the browser toolchain
steps.question: Which packages make the screens and the journey possible?
explanation: React renders screens, Vite serves the browser app, and playwright-core drives Chrome in the real browser check. The @types packages let TypeScript check React names.

At the practice root, run npm install --save-exact react@19.3.0 react-dom@19.3.0, then npm install --save-dev --save-exact vite@7.3.6 @vitejs/plugin-react@4.7.0 @types/react@19.3.0 @types/react-dom@19.3.0 playwright-core@1.63.0. These versions match the reference lockfile.

Add dev:client as vite --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173, test:ui as vitest run test/ui.test.tsx, and test:browser as node test/browser/run.mjs. Later lessons add each new UI test to test:ui and extend the browser runner.

vocabulary.meaning: A package the project runs with, installed by npm and recorded in package.json.
A package used only for building, testing, or serving during development.

hints: Goal: install the seven exact versions and add three named scripts.
Relevant value: npm ls --depth=0 prints the installed package versions.
Analogous example: like the M01 package list, each named dependency has one job.
Walkthrough: run the runtime install, run the development-tool install, edit scripts, and confirm package-lock.json is created.

steps.title: Point Vite at the client folder
steps.question: Where does the browser entry page live?
explanation: Create vite.config.ts at the practice root. Set root to src/client so Vite serves index.html beside the client files. Add the React plugin, output built files to ../../dist-client, and use port 5173 for dev:client.

Add a proxy for /practice-decision (the isolated validation lesson) and /game-decision (the identity-protected game route) to http://127.0.0.1:3002. The browser calls one local origin; Vite forwards either request to Nest. This avoids a cross-origin workaround.

vocabulary.meaning: A local forwarder: Vite passes one request to the server and returns its answer.

hints: Goal: root, React plugin, build output, client port, and both API proxy paths appear in vite.config.ts.
Relevant value: npx vite --version prints 7.3.6; Vite later prints http://127.0.0.1:5173/.
Analogous example: like tsconfig for tsc, vite.config.ts tells Vite which folder and tools to use.
Walkthrough: create the config at the project root; make the output path relative to src/client; forward both /practice-decision and /game-decision to port 3002.

steps.title: Scripts name the journey
steps.question: Which commands run the journey?
explanation: Five taught scripts with fixed roles. dev:server builds everything and serves the built client plus API on port 3002 (read its ready line). dev:client runs Vite on port 5173 for UI iteration with the fake transport. test:service runs the server suites. test:ui runs the client unit suites. test:browser orchestrates the full journey through run.mjs. Ports and ready output were checked in rehearsal.
hints: Name the five scripts.
Find the ports.
Compare with npm scripts so far.
Read the expected result before you change code.

steps.title: Run each script once
explanation: Start dev:server and read its ready line, then stop it. Start dev:client, open the printed URL, and see the page. Run test:service, test:ui, and test:browser separately so each failure points at its layer.

hints: Run one suite at a time.

steps.title: Teach one command to run the journey
steps.question: What does test:browser do in order?
explanation: Edit test/browser/run.mjs so test:browser starts both processes: the Nest API on port 3002 and Vite on port 5173. Wait for each ready line, pass the Vite URL as BASE_URL, run the named spec, then stop both processes even if a test fails.
Vite forwards /practice-decision to the API, so the page keeps one local URL. The local-game.spec.ts uses a real browser and real HTTP; the fake Judge stays labeled as a fake.

vocabulary.meaning: A script that runs other commands in order and reports one result.

hints: Goal: runner starts API and client, waits for both, runs the requested spec, then closes both.
Relevant value: the spec opens BASE_URL and gets an HTTP response through Vite proxy.
Analogous example: like two C processes with separate jobs, the server and browser client have separate ports.
Walkthrough: extend the existing runner with the server process and proxy path; use finally to stop both child processes.

files.owner: test/browser/ owns browser process setup and cleanup.
files.change: Start both services, set BASE_URL from Vite readiness, run the named spec, and stop both services.
files.pattern: Keep separate child handles; terminate both in finally and propagate the spec exit code.

steps.title: Complete the browser journey
steps.question: Does the browser complete a 1v1 loop with a failure included?
explanation: Practice paths: src/client/Arena.tsx, test/browser/local-game.spec.ts (plus the runner from the previous step). The spec uses vitest with playwright-core: it requires BASE_URL, launches Chrome (channel chrome, stock Chromium fallback), and drives verdict, failure diagnostic, keyboard, and narrow viewport.
hints: Goal: served Arena page completes problem, Run, failed request with diagnostic, keyboard path, and narrow layout.
Relevant value: npm run test:browser performs the whole orchestration; the spec alone needs BASE_URL.
Analogous example: like the course's own browser tests, drive real pages.
Walkthrough: assemble Arena from prior panels; write the spec with BASE_URL from the environment; fail fast without it.
